### Audit each option before ranking
Break each choice into its core claim and every added clause, and verify each independently under the stated hypotheses. For an “if and only if” or complete classification, establish both directions; a sufficient case alone does not establish necessity. Check the exact domain and scope of every component: existence does not by itself establish uniqueness, global scope, endpoint regularity, or other added properties. Rank only options whose full claims are established; stronger or more detailed wording is not evidence.

For almost-everywhere claims, preserve the specified reference measure. A set null for ambient Lebesgue measure may carry the probability measure used on a restricted locus; use the measure specified for that locus rather than silently switching measures.

For compactness and limit questions, check each part of the conclusion separately: convergence of parameters or spaces does not by itself establish convergence of metrics or inheritance of properties by the limit. Preserve exact limit qualifiers, such as locally versus globally homogeneous, and assert only properties proved to persist.
